findings.text: blocking: neither new profile declares a [slurm] section, so SlurmSettings defaults apply and both resolve to port None, gpus 4, cpus 30, memory 640G; at head tests/test_agent.py:355 test_every_profile_declares_a_distinct_port fails (assert all(port is not None)) and tests/test_agent.py:853 test_every_full_gpu_serve_leaves_reservation_headroom fails naming kimi-k3 and mimo-v2-6-pro at 4 GPUs / 30 cores, while both pass at base faa32881 with 4 passed EXIT=0, and cpus 30 on a device-resident vLLM profile is exactly the neighbour-starving topology that test exists to prevent.

non-blocking: the assertion compares the rendered script against site.model_dir(profile), the very function generate_download_script uses to fill MODEL_DIR, so both sides move together and a regression in model_dir leaves the assertion true; the independent half of that claim is the weights_slug check on :107.

non-blocking: the topology check inspects only the literal top-level key "slurm" and the keys under [engine], so a topology declared at top level (gpus, port, tensor_parallel) or in a new section such as [serving] would pass a test whose name claims no serving topology is declared.

non-blocking: the pin-reaches-transfer assertion duplicates the contract tests/test_agent_dspark_profile.py:287 already owns through an hf stub, and duplicates it more weakly, matching text in the script rather than the argv actually handed to the fetcher.

non-blocking: the gate log's revision header names faa328816dcaed3f7ffd9e9631d5e7d9db20e06a, the base, because the suite ran before the commit that carries the files it exercises, so a reader cannot tell from the log that the tested tree is the committed head 81de3fc2.
